Triggers.value: A specific taste associated with the event

Threat.value: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Memory.value: I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it

issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a patient whose indexed trauma is childhood physical abuse by a caregiver, 'comments on sexual violence' is not a clinically coherent trigger unless there is additional sexual-trauma history. The other trigger items (taste, sweat/body odour) can plausibly fit sensory reminders of physical abuse, but this specific sexual-trauma cue is hard to reconcile with the stated trauma type and the rest of the profile.

vignette: Meera, a 30-year-old South Asian woman and software engineer, has been struggling with persistent symptoms that stem from her traumatic childhood experience of physical abuse by her caregiver. Since she was young, Meera’s life has been marked by the lingering aftermath of these experiences, which have significantly impacted her daily functioning and well-being. One of the most potent triggers for Meera is a specific taste that brings back vivid memories of the abuse—this particular flavor is often associated with meals prepared during those traumatic times. The smell of sweat or body odour also serves as a powerful reminder, particularly in crowded office environments where she works among her colleagues. Additionally, the scent of alcohol, reminiscent of the caregiver’s intoxication, can provoke intense distress. Meera has come to believe that these triggers are signs of impending danger and have led her into a cycle of heightened vigilance and threat monitoring. Whenever she encounters any of these cues, whether it be the taste or smell, Meera feels an overwhelming sense of fear and anxiety. This often results in sleep disturbances—trouble falling asleep or staying asleep—as she is constantly on guard for any potential threats. The impact of these triggers extends to her memory recall as well. When confronted with one of these triggers, Meera’s memories become disorganized and confused; she struggles to put them in the right sequence. The emotional intensity of these memories overwhelms her, often forcing her to push them away before they are fully processed. This fragmented recollection further contributes to her inability to relax even when she knows she is in a safe place, reinforcing her sense of threat. This cycle has become increasingly self-perpetuating over time. Meera’s memory issues have compounded the distress caused by her triggers, as she continually grapples with incomplete and chaotic memories. The fragmented nature of these recollections makes it difficult for her to fully process what happened, leading to a persistent state of hypervigilance. In her role as a software engineer, the office environment can be particularly challenging. Crowded meetings or social gatherings often trigger her memories, making it hard for Meera to focus on work and form meaningful connections with colleagues. Her fear that someone might recognize these triggers and judge her exacerbates her anxiety. Meera’s marriage has also been affected by these symptoms. While she is deeply committed to her husband, the constant threat monitoring makes it difficult for her to fully relax in their home or engage in activities together. She repeatedly checks doors and windows to ensure they are locked, finding solace in this ritual but feeling an underlying sense of unease. The culmination of these experiences has led Meera to seek help now more than ever before. Her husband’s encouragement and her growing realization that she cannot manage the symptoms alone have propelled her towards therapy. What frightens her most is the prospect of living with this constant threat indefinitely, while what she hopes for most is finding a way to reclaim control over her memories and fears, enabling her to live a more peaceful life. In essence, Meera’s narrative illustrates how the interplay between triggers, memory issues, and threat monitoring has created a complex web of symptoms that have significantly impacted her daily functioning and well-being. The cycle of distress is palpable as each component reinforces the others, driving her towards a place where she can finally find relief and healing.
